title: Space time coordination dynamics in bask
universal_lens: Space-time coordination dynamics in basketball integrates geometric centering, stretch dispersion, and phase locking across longitudinal and lateral team behaviors. Relative-phase dynamics in spatial centre coordination during shot attempts reveal disrupted in-phase patterns linked to team strategies and possession shifts.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference models team spatial centers and stretch indices to predict in-phase coordination stability in basketball dynamics. Bayesian inference models lateral and longitudinal relative-phase disruptions as stochastic predictors of shot classification and possession events using conformal predictive distributions.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning maps team movement transitions via phase relations and binary stretch differences for tactical state shifts. Situational reasoning engine maps real-time relative-phase anomalies to state transitions in team coordination, enabling tactical response prediction via kernel-based dynamical systems.

This suggests that teams may exhibit synchronized movement along the court's length but less so across width. Phase locking mechanisms are introduced as a way to measure coordination fidelity, particularly between opposing teams. Binary representations of stretch index differences reveal transitions between stable behavioral patterns, indicating that team dynamics shift in response to possession changes. These insights support a broader theoretical framework where complex systems—such as basketball teams—exhibit emergent properties at multiple scales. The study builds upon prior work on player dyad interactions and extends it to inter-team coordination. It also highlights the importance of reciprocity in team expansion and contraction during possession transitions. The implications suggest that strategic positioning and movement synchronization are not only influenced by individual skill but also by systemic coupling effects within and between teams.
